\n\n

\n\n

After x days, B left work, and A joined with C.

\n\n

(A + C) completed the remaining in (x - 41) days.

\n\n

(B + C) : (A + C) = 19 : 6

\n\n

Calculation:

\n\n

A complete the work = 20 / (1/5) = 20 × 5 = 100 days

\n\n

B complete the work = 36/3 × 100 = 120 days

\n\n

C complete the work = 160/8 × 100 = 200 days

\n\n

Total work = LCM of (100, 120, 200) = 600

\n\n

According to the question,

\n\n
⇒ 600 = (B+C)x + (A+C)(x-41)
\n⇒ 600 = 8x + 9(x-41)
\n\n
⇒ 600 = 17x - 369
\n\n
⇒ 17x = 600 + 369
\n\n
⇒ x = 969/17 = 57
\nNow, In 2x days, C completes the work per day.
\n\n
⇒ \\(\\frac{2x}{600}× efficiency \\)
\n⇒ \\(\\frac{2×57}{600}× 3\\) \\(= \\frac{57}{100}\\)
\n\n
\n
∴ C alone can complete \\(\\frac{57}{100}\\)of the work in 2x days.

Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

\n\n

Sanchit stands by his friends through thick and thin.

\n", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "In winter and summer"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "In favourable situations&nbsp;"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "In crowded areas"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "Under all circumstances&nbsp;"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "4", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

The correct answer is Option (4) i.e. 'Under all circumstances'.

\n\n

Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t
  • The idiom Through thick and thin means: In both good times and bad times (हर परिस्थिति में)\n\n\t
      \n\t\t
    • Example: She has supported me through thick and thin.
      • \n\t
    \n\t
    • \n\t
  • Under all circumstances: (हर स्थिति में) - Regardless of the situation or difficulty.
    • \n\t
  • This option directly reflects the idiom's meaning related to unwavering support or allegiance in every situation.
    • \n
\n\n

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Under all circumstances'.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n
    \n\t
  • In winter and summer: Literal seasons, not related to the abstract meaning of support and loyalty conveyed by the idiom.
    • \n\t
  • In favourable situations: (अनुकूल स्थितियों में) - Only when things are going well, which does not fully capture the idiom's encompassing intent.
    • \n\t
  • In crowded areas: (भीड़-भाड़ वाले क्षेत्रों में) - A literal physical space, unrelated to the concept of enduring support implied by the idiom.
    • \n

\n\nSelect the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word.

\n", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "Disgust"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "Despise"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "Care"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "Wish"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "4", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

The correct answer is Option 4) "Wish".

\n\n

Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t
  • In this context she has no interest or wish for money.
    • \n\t
  • Desire: (इच्छा) - A strong feeling of wanting to have something or wishing for something to happen.\n\t
      \n\t\t
    • Example: She has no desire for money.
      • \n\t
    \n\t
    • \n\t
  • Wish: (इच्छा) - A desire or hope for something to happen.\n\t
      \n\t\t
    • Example: His only wish was to see his daughter happy.
      • \n\t
    \n\t
    • \n\t
  • Hence, the correct meaning of "desire" in this context is "Wish".
    • \n
\n\n

Therefore, the correct answer is "Wish".

\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n
    \n\t
  • Disgust: (घृणा) - A strong feeling of disapproval or revulsion.
    • \n\t
  • Despise: (तिरस्कार करना) - Feel contempt or a deep repugnance for.
    • \n\t
  • Care: (परवाह करना) - Feel concern or interest; attach importance to something.

The correct answer is Option (4) i.e. 'However'.

\n\n

Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t
  • "However" is used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has been said previously.
    • \n\t
  • In this context, it introduces the surprising or contrasting fact that not all swans are white, following the mention of their distinctive features.
    • \n\t
  • The passage contrasts the general expectation of swans being white with the existence of the Black Swan, which is black, making "However" the appropriate choice to show this contrast.
    • \n
\n\n

Therefore, the correct answer is 'However'.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n
    \n\t
  • Option (1) "Consequently" implies a result or an effect stemming from what has been mentioned before, which does not suit the context of introducing a contrast.
    • \n\t
  • Option (2) "Because" introduces a reason or explanation, not a contrasting statement.
    • \n\t
  • Option (3) "Formerly" suggests something related to the past, which does not fit the context of contrasting the color of swans.
    • \n
\n\n

Complete Passage is: Swans are large waterbirds that belong to the family Anatidae, which also includes ducks and geese. They are known for their beauty and grace and are often used as symbols of love, fidelity, and elegance. They are also famous for their distinctive features, such as their long necks, large wingspans, and striking white feathers. However, not all swan species are white; the Black Swan, ________, has black feathers with a red bill. Swans are found on every continent and are known for their strong pair bonds. They mate for life and can live up to 20 years. Keep the other blank-in-the-blank condition.

        \n", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "convinced to speaking&nbsp;"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "reassured of speaking"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "assured of speaking"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "confident in speaking"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "4", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

        The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'confident in speaking'.

        \n\n

        Key Points

        \n\n
          \n\t
        • "Confident in speaking" is the correct grammatical structure when expressing proficiency or self-assurance in an ability, such as language skills.
          • \n\t
        • The preposition "in" is commonly used with the adjective "confident" to describe certainty in one's capabilities in a particular area or activity.\n\t
            \n\t\t
          • Example: Alex was confident in speaking during the meeting.
            • \n\t
          \n\t
          • \n\t
        • The phrase fits naturally into the context of developing language skills, making it a suitable substitution for "confident to speak".
          • \n
        \n\n

        Therefore, the correct answer is- You can become confident in speaking English within one year.

        \n\n

        Additional Information

        \n\n
          \n\t
        • Convinced to speaking (Option 1) uses incorrect grammatical structure and implies persuasion rather than self-assurance.
          • \n\t
        • Reassured of speaking (Option 2) suggests being given confidence by someone else, which doesn't fit the context of personal development in language proficiency.
          • \n\t
        • Assured of speaking (Option 3) also doesn't fit as neatly as "confident in speaking". It more so implies a guarantee from another source rather than an internal sense of confidence.
          • \n

            \n", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "Genuine"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "Fake"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "Basic"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "Different"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "2", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

            The correct answer is' Fake.'

            \n\n

            Key Points

            \n\n
              \n\t
            • Authentic (असली): This word means genuine, real, and of undisputed origin. It implies something is true and not a copy or imitation.\n\n\t
                \n\t\t
              • Example: "The chef uses only authentic ingredients in her recipes."
                • \n\t
              \n\t
              • \n\t
            • Fake (नकली): This word means not genuine, false, or a copy of something real. It is the direct opposite of authentic, indicating something is not genuine or true.\n\t
                \n\t\t
              • Example: "The online store was selling fake designer clothing."
                • \n\t
              \n\t
              • \n\t
            • Hence, "fake" is the most appropriate antonym of "authentic".
              • \n
            \n\n

            Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

            \n\n

            Additional Information

            \n\n
              \n\t
            • Genuine (असली): While seemingly close, "genuine" is actually a synonym of "authentic," not an antonym.
              • \n\t
            • Basic (मूल): This word simply means fundamental or essential, and doesn't convey the opposite meaning of genuine or real.
              • \n\t
            • Different (अलग): This word simply means not the same, but doesn't necessarily imply a lack of genuineness. It can be different but still be authentic.
              • \n

                  The correct answer is Option (1) i.e. 'for example'.Key Points

                  \n\n
                    \n\t
                  • "For example" is used to introduce an instance or an illustration of a broader category or statement made previously.
                    • \n\t
                  • In this context, it serves to provide a specific example (the Black Swan) that contrasts with the general statement about swans being recognized for their striking white feathers.
                    • \n\t
                  • The passage is illustrating an exception to the common perception of swans with the mention of the Black Swan's unique coloration, making "for example" the appropriate choice to introduce this specific case.
                    • \n
                  \n\n

                  Therefore, the correct answer is 'for example'.Additional Information

                  \n\n
                    \n\t
                  • Option (2) "of course" is typically used to emphasize something that is considered obvious or well-known, which does not suit the introduction of a specific contrasting example.
                    • \n\t
                  • Option (3) "after all" is usually used to add information that confirms or goes back to something previously said, but it does not aptly introduce an example.
                    • \n\t
                  • Option (4) "in addition" is used to add extra information to what has been previously stated, rather than to introduce a specific example that contrasts with what has been mentioned.
                    • \n
                  \n\n

                  Complete Passage is: Swans are large waterbirds that belong to the family Anatidae, which also includes ducks and geese. They are known for their beauty and grace and are often used as symbols of love, fidelity, and elegance. They are also famous for their distinctive features, such as their long necks, large wingspans, and striking white feathers. However, not all swan species are white; the Black Swan, for example, has black feathers with a red bill. Swans are found on every continent and are known for their strong pair bonds. They mate for life and can live up to 20 years. Keep the other blank-in-the-blank condition.
